headline: Tabled FY27 budget until November, when the state match is announced; also tabled June minutes approval and officer elections.
summary: Members discussed FY27 applications, including Amerige Field restoration and First Parish Church façade work, but took no funding votes. The FY27 budget was tabled until November, when the state will announce its match. Members also agreed to have the CPC Manager present a preservation monitoring strategy to the Historical Commission.

Tabled the election of CPA officers until new members are seated, approved unanimously.

decision_titles: Preservation restriction monitoring strategy for First Parish Church
plain_text:
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 1 
  
  
  
   
  
  
Community Preservation Committee  
 
 
Malden City Hall Room #105 
Broadcast live and recorded on Teams 
September 16, 2026 | 6:00 p.m. 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Committee Members in Attendance: Rachael Running, Chair, Sam Watters, Vice Chair, Inna Babitskaya, 
Jamie Kendall, Monique Ching, Brendan Brett, Cayla Paulding 
Committee Members Absent: Ronnie Raj Verma 
CPC Manager: Daniel Koff  
 
1. Meeting Called to Order 
Running called the meeting to order at 6:07p.m and conducted attendance.  
 
2. Approval of CPC Monthly Meeting minutes from June 17, 2026 
Running tabled the approval of the June meeting minutes.  
 
3. FY27 Budget 
Running tabled this item until November after which point the state will announce the FY27 match. For 
now, CPC will operate with its current budget that was approved by City Council at the end of FY26 
which reflects CPC’s conservative estimate for its FY27 budget that was submitted by the March 31 
deadline, before the state match estimate was announced by DOR. The difference in the state match 
will be approximately $28,000.00. This amount, plus actual revenue received that was above and
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 2 
beyond CPC’s estimates for the past two years may be corrected after the state match is announced in 
November.  
No further motions were made. 
 
4. Preservation Restriction for First Parish Church 
Running invited Koff to inform CPC about the status of the Preservation Restriction for First Parish 
Church. 
Koff explained the meetings that were conducted over the summer with the Solicitor and Historical 
Commission, as well as a Preservation Consultant and representatives from First Parish. The Consultant, 
Shantia Anderheggen of Preservation Strategies, discussed a few ways that First Parish could proceed 
with the creation of a Preservation Restriction and ultimately recommended that the parties wait for the 
project of repointing the entire façade to be complete before establishing the Preservation Restriction. 
In the meantime, she recommended that CPC and the Parish enter into a Letter of Agreement 
confirming this intention. Because First Parish plans to continue applying to CPC each year while it raises 
funding from other sources to complete the project, entering into one Preservation Restriction will be 
able to cover all of that work.  
Alternatively, CPC could demand a new Preservation Restriction be created for each award, but that 
could become costly and legally confusing to have multiple restrictions in effect.  
Running opened the floor for discussion. 
Watters agreed that creating a Letter of Agreement would be a good strategy because it would be 
future proof in that it doesn’t commit CPC to allocate additional funding. 
Running invited Koff to explain the consultants’ next proposal to monitor the Preservation Restriction.  
Koff explained that Anderheggen recommended creating a survey that a City staff member can 
complete each year to generate a status report that can be provided to the Historical Commission (as 
the owner of the Restriction). The status of the project could be measured against photographs taken 
when the work is complete.  Anderheggen provided CPC with a consultant services proposal to create 
this survey.  
Babistkaya advocated for hiring a preservation consultant for an additional scope of work in the future. 
Running offered to potentially hire a consultant every few years as opposed to hiring a consultant 
annually. 
Babitskaya suggested that the Historical Commission is next week, and as a next step the CPC Manager 
could attend to present the consultant’s proposals. Koff was unable to attend the following week, so it 
was agreed that he would attend at their next meeting in October.  
Kendall inquired as to what other communities do in terms of PR’s and monitoring. Koff explained that 
Somerville has created a knot with over 400 historical districts and required permanent historic 
restrictions to be put in place with all properties that received CPA Funds. Other communities do not 
monitor their preservation restrictions at all. Kendall clarified that having a checklist that a CPA Manager
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 3 
could fill out would constitute a more robust monitoring system compared to other communities in the 
state.  
Running explained that there may be a middle ground for not being responsible having experts oversee 
these projects and not. 
CPC agreed as a next step for the CPC Manager to present the proposed monitoring strategy to the 
Historical Commission and report back. 
 
5. FY27 Applications 
Running explained that at this point in the application review process, CPC discusses the merits of each 
project, and identifies questions to ask each applicant when they are notified of their Public Hearing 
date in the fall.  
0039_Affordable Housing Trust 
Babitskaya explained that the City is considering lowering the inclusionary zoning requirement of 15% to 
10% in order to incentivize development given changes to market pressure. She inquired as to why the 
request to CPC is increased when the City is considering requiring less of an investment from 
developers. Ching clarified that lowering the IZ requirement would increase the need from CPC because 
the Trust will be receiving less funding from developers.  
Running explained that the difficult economy speaks to the need for more affordable housing and 
lowering the requirements to incentivize more development.  
Babitskaya inquired as to how many units have been created. Koff explained that there are 20-21 units 
at 213 Main Street and 99 units at Overlook Ridge. 
Ching requested clarity on the budget that shows their cost share at $531,000, yet those numbers are 
varied from the amounts provided in t. 
 
0040_Amerige Field Restoration 
Running summarized that OSPCD is requesting $750,000 to restore the park, including fixing drainage, 
installing a new playground, making areas ADA accessible, renovating the courts, etc. Running explained 
that this request represents a new approach by OSPCD to focus on renovating one park. 
Babitskaya inquired as to whether there is an itemized budget. CPC confirmed that there is a budget in 
the memo from Shadley Associates that was included in as an attachment to the application 
(FY27_0040_090226_Amerige Park_CPC Application Memo_4329) 
Members expressed an interest in learning more about what might be included in the project.  
Brett expressed reservations to approve such a large funding request without having a plan in place.  
Ching inquired as to whether the project could be broken up into phases, including a design phase.
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 4 
Ching and Kendall discussed the potential implications of using a PARC grant as a matching source, and 
requested more information about it, including the timeline for application and receipt of matching 
funds.  
Kendall expressed her opinion that the playground is in good shape, even if it is a little outdated and not 
ADA accessible. Kendall inquired as to whether there are ways to make selective interventions to make it 
ADA accessible without leveling the playground.  
Brett asked OSPCD to prioritize the elements given potential budget constraints. 
Members inquired whether improvements to the hard and soft surface play areas would constitute 
regular maintenance versus a significant capital improvement worthy of CPA Funds. 
 
0041_Florence Street Pocket Park 
Running summarized that the Florence Street Pocket Park will improve the amenities in the area. This 
project does not come with a cost share, so if it is not funded by CPC it will not move forward.  
Running inquired as to whether the planning team would conduct a community meeting as part of the 
project development. 
Kendall requested a more detailed budget, particularly the line item for demolition.  
Brett inquired as to whether the work would be completed by City employees and how that might impact 
the budget. 
 
0042_First Parish in Malden 
Running summarized that the request for $500,000 is to continue rehabilitating the façade of the 
Church. In FY26 CPC awarded $250k to the project. This request would fund additional portions of the 
building. Ching pointed out that the cost share on their budget includes the FY26 CPA funding, even 
though it is still from CPC. She requested that. 
Running expressed that it is equally worthy from last year, but it comes in as a large request. Kendall and 
Brett agreed. 
Watters agreed with all and requested for the Parish update their budget to show that CPC’s FY26 award 
does not contribute to their cost share.  
 
0043_Malden Rental Assistance Program 
Running summarized that the ABCD project would renew funding for the Start Secure project to provide 
move-in costs, first, and last months rent, and salary to their housing coordinator.  
Running would like to hear a more extensive project update to better understand their success in Malden 
and other cities where the program is run.
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 5 
Ching inquired as to how they came up with a specific amount, specifically with the $75k that would be 
allocated to direct financial assistance.  
Running requested to learn more about the duties of the administrators of the program.  
Ching requested to learn more information about the steps in the review process to help people access 
the funding support. 
Kendall inquired as to what they may do if they do not identify the exact demographics of people they 
expect to assist.  
Ching inquired as to the reasons why the program took years to spend down.  
 
 
0044_Housing Subsidy for Older Adults 
Running summarized that this grant would support elders to stay in their home with rental assistance.  
Kendall expressed appreciation for their report showing the number of people assisted, that they 
started at a lower amount and are requesting additional funding for it to continue.  
 
0045_Malden River Boathouse 
Brett inquired as to whether the boathouse would provide access to boats for the public. 
 
Scheduling Public Hearings 
Running advocated for scheduling the housing and historic preservation projects on October 21, and the 
open space and recreation projects on November 18 or 16 (to be confirmed in October).  
 
6. CPA Election of Officers 
Running opened the floor to anyone who wanted to run for office, or to table the item until next 
meeting. No one expressed interest in running for a leadership position. A conversation ensued about 
the number of new CPA members who should be arriving this year. 
Watters made a motion to table this item until new members are seated. Seconded by Running. 
Approved unanimously.  
 
7. CPA Ordinance Updates 
Running summarized that the City is considering ordinance changes to govern CPC appointments and 
term limits.
CPC Meeting Minutes  pg. 6 
Brett advocated for continuing to have members distributed across the City. Kendall agreed that 
geographic diversity is important. Running believes that softer language could be included so that 
geographic distribution is encouraged but may not be a hard requirement.  
Brett inquired as to whether candidates would still be interviewed by the Personnel Committee of the 
City Council.  
Kendall expressed that the term going from 2-3 years makes sense. Brett confirmed that the first year 
there is a large learning curve.  
Running expressed that it has been difficult to identify a Chair since it is a lot of extra unpaid work.  
Watters made a motion to adjourn. Seconded by Running. Approved unanimously.  
 
8. Other Business 
Running invited everyone to the Malden River Works grand opening on October 4th, and expressed that 
it would be helpful to know who can attend.  
 
9. Adjournment of CPC Monthly Meeting 
Brett made a motion to adjourn. Seconded by Ching. Approved unanimously.
